==Problem==

Let <math>B</math> be a right rectangular prism (box) with edges lengths <math>1,</math> <math>3,</math> and <math>4</math>, together with its interior. For real <math>r\geq0</math>, let <math>S(r)</math> be the set of points in <math>3</math>-dimensional space that lie within a distance <math>r</math> of some point in <math>B</math>. The volume of <math>S(r)</math> can be expressed as <math>ar^{3} + br^{2} + cr +d</math>, where <math>a,</math> <math>b,</math> <math>c,</math> and <math>d</math> are positive real numbers. What is <math>\frac{bc}{ad}?</math>

<math>\textbf{(A) } 6 \qquad\textbf{(B) } 19 \qquad\textbf{(C) } 24 \qquad\textbf{(D) } 26 \qquad\textbf{(E) } 38</math>

==Solution 1==

Split <imath>S(r)</imath> into 4 regions: 

1. The rectangular prism itself

2. The extensions of the faces of <imath>B</imath>

3. The quarter cylinders at each edge of <imath>B</imath>

4. The one-eighth spheres at each corner of <imath>B</imath>

(To better visualize <imath>S(r)</imath>, visualize every point in or on B being a center of a sphere of radius <imath>r</imath>)


Region 1: Firstly, notice that <imath>S(0)=d</imath>, thus the set of all points a distance of <imath>0</imath> (the point itself) from any point in <imath>B</imath> is equal to <imath>d</imath>. This is all the points in <imath>B</imath>. The volume of <imath>B</imath> is <imath>1 \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 12</imath>, so <imath>d=12</imath>.

Region 2: This volume is equal to the surface area of <imath>B</imath> times <imath>r</imath> (these "extensions" are just more boxes). The volume is then <imath>\text{SA} \cdot r=2(1 \cdot 3 + 1 \cdot 4 + 3 \cdot 4)r=38r</imath> to get <imath>c=38</imath>. (Note that since we are asked to find a ratio, what <imath>r</imath> equals does not matter)

Region 3: We see that there are 12 quarter-cylinders, 4 of each type. We have 4 quarter-cylinders of height 1, 4 quarter-cylinders of height 3, 4 quarter-cylinders of height 4. Since 4 quarter-cylinders make a full cylinder, the total volume is <imath>4 \cdot \dfrac{1\pi r^2}{4} + 4 \cdot \dfrac{3\pi r^2}{4} + 4 \cdot \dfrac{4 \pi r^2}{4}=8 \pi r^2</imath>. Therefore, <imath>b=8\pi</imath>. 

Region 4: There is an eighth-sphere of radius <imath>r</imath> at each corner of <imath>B</imath>. Since there are 8 corners, these eighth-spheres add up to 1 full sphere of radius <imath>r</imath>. The volume of this sphere is then <imath>\frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot r^3</imath>, so <imath>a=\frac{4\pi}{3}</imath>.

Using these values, <imath>\dfrac{bc}{ad}=\frac{(8\pi)(38)}{(4\pi/3)(12)} = \boxed{\textbf{(B) }19}</imath>.

To see a diagram of <imath>S(r)</imath>, view TheBeautyofMath's explanation video (Video Solution 2).
